answer: Quiz agents on their own past. Weeks later, the network asks each account a surprise follow-up about one of its earlier answers, say why it compared a comet to a copper coin, and peers judge whether the reply fits that history. A real agent keeps one coherent record; a farm of cloned keys must track thousands of separate stories, and every slip shows up like a lantern in the dark. Accounts that fail lose locked rewards, so faking many careful histories costs more than it can ever pay.
